claims.claim: notes/note-1.md gates project-level impersonation rollout on 'the diff story is fixed,' and note-1 treats T-26271 (root-caused as the impersonated SA lacking patch on cluster-scoped resources) as that story. But tickets/T-28695.md shows the actual gap is structural: on external clusters the diff path never honors AppProject destinationServiceAccounts at all (only sync does), so every new resource kind forces another unbounded patch grant onto the narrow cluster credential. Documenting T-26271's root cause does not close that gap, and no owner is named for making diff honor destinationServiceAccounts, so the rollout gate has no accountable path to becoming true.

strategy.md states that ordered/automated deletion of ApplicationSet-generated children 'will not be implemented' and that teardown must remain a manual, one-Application-at-a-time operator action. prd-progressive-sync-deletion.md proposes exactly the opposite — an automated deletionOrder (AllAtOnce/Reverse) strategy field — and tickets/T-28511.md's reproduction confirms it is already shipped and in use, with the Reverse ordering mode implicated in a delete/recreate incident loop. notes/note-2.md names this same PRD-vs-strategy disagreement directly and says it 'needs an owner. not deciding here,' leaving a shipped, incident-causing feature in open conflict with the roadmap's stated scope with no one accountable to resolve it.

notes/note-2.md's incident-review restriction — hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until a wave-restart debounce exists, to be written onto T-27949 — collides with tickets/T-24578.md's open request to add Source Hydrator support to ApplicationSets specifically so RollingSync-based deletion ordering can be used across multi-cluster deprovisioning. T-24578 shows no awareness of the debounce restriction, so the feature combination it asks for is exactly what note-2 just forbade for pilot repos.

tickets/T-28927.md's maturity-review scope call freezes strategy.rollingSync.steps (the matchExpressions-per-step list) as Progressive Sync's backward-compatible v1 shape once Stable ships, requiring any change to how a step is expressed to land as a new field beforehand rather than an in-place restructuring afterward. tickets/T-28755.md's parallel-steps proposal sketches restructuring that same steps list in place (nesting 'parallel:' entries directly inside rollingSync.steps) as one of its two API options — the exact kind of change T-28927 says must land before the freeze — with no decision recorded reconciling the two before Stable promotion proceeds.

strategy.md commits application controller capacity this quarter to closing the Progressive Sync Stable-promotion punch list and names the sharding pair as the same pair doing that work, stating sharding (also on the v2.4+ roadmap) 'will not start until the Stable promotion closes.' tickets/T-28927.md, which defines that punch list, is still working an open scope call (freezing rollingSync.steps) that collides with tickets/T-28755.md's proposal — so the punch list's closure, and therefore sharding's start date, depends on resolving a design disagreement that has no target date attached to it.
